newsitem.title: SUDAN: Sudan says abiding by agreement with Uganda.
newsitem.headline: Sudan says abiding by agreement with Uganda.

text.p: Sudan said on Thursday it was abiding by its border agreement with Uganda and that a monitoring group would soon start work ensuring that neither government helps rebels operating in the area.
The Minister of Culture and Information, Brigadier al-Tayeb Ibrahim Mohamed Khair, told state radio: "Sudan is keen to implement the agreement on normalisation of relations."
"Sudan has not contravened any of the articles in the agreement... It has not allowed its territory or border to be used by any fronts hostile to Uganda," he added.
Sudan had accused Uganda of helping the Sudan People's Liberation Army, the main rebel group in south Sudan.
Uganda in turn said the Sudanese government was helping the Lord's Resistance Army, a Christian fundamentalist group active among the Acholi of northern Uganda.

Sudan and Uganda signed the original agreement in September as a result of mediation by Iranian President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani but the monitoring group, to include representatives of Sudan, Uganda, Iran, Libya and Malawi, has not started work.
"It (the group) will begin its work soon to stop any violations in the border areas by any side," said Khair.
Arab press reports from east Africa say Uganda has decided to pull out of the negotiations on the grounds that the Sudanese side are not respecting the September agreement.
They quoted a Ugandan Foreign Ministry as saying Uganda would not sign a final peace agreement at a ceremony scheduled to take place in the Iranian capital Tehran next Monday.
Brigadier Khair did not refer to such an agreement.

Under the September agreement, the two governments also agreed to stop hostile propaganda campaigns, destroy rebel positions and supply centres, move all refugees and rebels at least 100 km (60 miles) inside the border and encourage the voluntary repatriation of refugees from the two countries.
